questions.stem: This sequence of diagrams depicts an embryologic process in the developing heart, involving the septum primum, septum secundum, endocardial cushions, and closure toward the foramen ovale. What process is being illustrated?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Development of the cardiac conduction system

choices.label: E
choices.text: Septation of the atria and ventricles

explanation.summary: Growth of the septum primum and secundum, fusion of the endocardial cushions, and formation of the interventricular septum divide the primitive heart into four chambers; the foramen ovale persists as a right-to-left shunt until birth.
explanation.whyCorrect: Growth of the septum primum and secundum, fusion of the endocardial cushions, and formation of the interventricular septum divide the primitive heart into four chambers; the foramen ovale persists as a right-to-left shunt until birth.

questions.stem: This cross-sectional diagram shows blood flow through the cardiac chambers, with arrows tracing the path. The blue-shaded chambers and vessels (right atrium, right ventricle, pulmonary trunk) carry what type of blood?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mixed venous and arterial blood of equal saturation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blood with the highest oxygen content in the circulation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deoxygenated blood returning to the lungs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oxygenated blood being delivered to the body

choices.label: E
choices.text: Blood that has just left the pulmonary veins

explanation.summary: The right side of the heart (blue) receives deoxygenated systemic venous blood via the vena cavae and pumps it through the pulmonary trunk/arteries to the lungs for oxygenation. The left side (pink) handles oxygenated blood returning via the pulmonary veins for systemic delivery.
explanation.whyCorrect: The right side of the heart (blue) receives deoxygenated systemic venous blood via the vena cavae and pumps it through the pulmonary trunk/arteries to the lungs for oxygenation. The left side (pink) handles oxygenated blood returning via the pulmonary veins for systemic delivery.

questions.stem: This sagittal cadaveric section shows scroll-like bony projections along the lateral wall of an air-filled cavity above the hard palate and teeth. These conchae (turbinates) line which cavity?

explanation.summary: The section is a midsagittal cut through the head showing the nasal cavity with its superior, middle, and inferior conchae on the lateral wall. The olfactory epithelium sits high in the roof of this cavity; the conchae warm, humidify, and filter inspired air.
explanation.whyCorrect: The section is a midsagittal cut through the head showing the nasal cavity with its superior, middle, and inferior conchae on the lateral wall. The olfactory epithelium sits high in the roof of this cavity; the conchae warm, humidify, and filter inspired air.

questions.stem: This diagram color-codes the body by lymphatic drainage territory. The yellow region drains into the thoracic duct. Which single body region does NOT drain via the thoracic duct?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Left side of the head and neck

choices.label: E
choices.text: Right side of the head/neck, right upper limb, and right thorax

explanation.summary: The thoracic duct drains the lower body plus the entire left upper quadrant into the left subclavian/internal jugular junction. Only the right upper quadrant (right head/neck, right arm, right hemithorax) drains via the separate right lymphatic duct into the right venous angle.
explanation.whyCorrect: The thoracic duct drains the lower body plus the entire left upper quadrant into the left subclavian/internal jugular junction. Only the right upper quadrant (right head/neck, right arm, right hemithorax) drains via the separate right lymphatic duct into the right venous angle.

questions.stem: This diagram shows the sympathetic trunk giving off the greater, lesser, and least splanchnic nerves that pass to ganglia near the aorta. What type of fibers do these splanchnic nerves carry toward the abdominal viscera?

explanation.summary: The thoracic and abdominal splanchnic nerves carry preganglionic sympathetic axons that pass through the sympathetic chain without synapsing and terminate in the prevertebral (collateral) ganglia - the celiac and related ganglia - shown near the aorta, where they synapse before reaching the gut.
explanation.whyCorrect: The thoracic and abdominal splanchnic nerves carry preganglionic sympathetic axons that pass through the sympathetic chain without synapsing and terminate in the prevertebral (collateral) ganglia - the celiac and related ganglia - shown near the aorta, where they synapse before reaching the gut.

questions.stem: This diagram shows a heart valve viewed from above with two leaflets (an anterior and a posterior leaflet) tethered by chordae tendineae to papillary muscles below. Which valve is depicted?

explanation.summary: A bileaflet atrioventricular valve (anterior and posterior leaflets) with chordae tendineae anchored to papillary muscles is the mitral valve. The tricuspid has three leaflets, and the aortic and pulmonic are semilunar (three-cusp) valves without chordae.
explanation.whyCorrect: A bileaflet atrioventricular valve (anterior and posterior leaflets) with chordae tendineae anchored to papillary muscles is the mitral valve. The tricuspid has three leaflets, and the aortic and pulmonic are semilunar (three-cusp) valves without chordae.
